gaps.sentence: Passengers ___ open the doors before the train stops completely.
gaps.hint: a safety rule that forbids something

gaps.sentence: The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better book now — the prices rise every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice, often with urgency: had better book.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not agree, but let us ask him anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility about the future: may not agree.

gaps.sentence: You ___ see a doctor about that cough; it has lasted three weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' gives advice or a recommendation: should see.
